title: Revenue From First-Time vs Repeat Purchases
description:
Split all orders into `'first'` (the customer's earliest order) and `'repeat'` (all subsequent orders). Show the order count and total revenue for each purchase type.

**Table: orders** — `order_id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `amount`

Output columns: `purchase_type`, `order_count`, `total_revenue`. Order by `purchase_type`.
solution_sql: WITH order_ranks AS (SELECT order_id, customer_id, amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) AS order_rank FROM orders) SELECT CASE WHEN order_rank = 1 THEN 'first' ELSE 'repeat' END AS purchase_type, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(amount) AS total_revenue FROM order_ranks GROUP BY CASE WHEN order_rank = 1 THEN 'first' ELSE 'repeat' END ORDER BY purchase_type;

test_cases.description: First purchases: 4 orders totalling 550; Repeat purchases: 5 orders totalling 900

hints: Use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) to number each customer's orders.
Label rows with order_rank = 1 as 'first' and all others as 'repeat' using CASE WHEN.
Then GROUP BY the purchase_type label to get total counts and revenue.
explanation: ROW_NUMBER assigns rank 1 to each customer's earliest order. First purchases: customer 1 (100), customer 2 (120), customer 3 (80), customer 4 (250) = 4 orders, total 550. Repeat purchases: customer 1 orders 2 & 3 (150+200=350), customer 3 orders 2 & 3 (160+90=250), customer 4 order 2 (300) = 5 orders, total 900.
